why_angle: The rival pages give only rated Wh and their own 75–85% assumptions. None prints a named lab's delivered-energy figure for any of the 1 kWh kit stations. This page ranks the kits on lab-measured AC energy (BLUETTI AC180 980–1,030 Wh against 850–910 Wh for the EcoFlow, Jackery and Anker units) and adds the low-load result of 530–620 Wh at about 34 W.

page.after:
What the differences mean

  • Share of the rating you actually get: AC180 980 ÷ 1,152 = 85% (Outdoor Life) and 1,030 ÷ 1,152 = 89% (StorageReview). S2000 Pro 920 ÷ 1,500 = 61% (StorageReview, 2023 unit).
  • Cost per delivered Wh: AC180 bundle $1,232 ÷ 980 Wh = $1.26. AC180 + 200 W kit plus a second SP200L, $1,168 ÷ 980 Wh = $1.19. S2000 Pro + SP037, $848 ÷ 920 Wh = $0.92.
  • Bundle against parts: at BLUETTI, $499 AC180 + 2 × $399 SP200L = $1,297 bought separately, so the $1,232 bundle saves $65. The $769 AC180 + 200 W kit + one $399 SP200L = $1,168, which is $64 under the bundle. At ALLPOWERS, the $399 P1800 + the $299 SP037 flash deal = $698, the kit price to the dollar, so that bundle saves nothing over the parts.
  • Fastest solar refill at full panel rating: AC180 1,152 Wh ÷ 400 W = 2.9 h. P1800 1,024 Wh ÷ 400 W = 2.6 h. Both are before charging losses.
  • Panel voltage the AC180 needs: 400 W ÷ 10 A = 40 V across the array.

How much energy a 1 kWh station really gives

A station's rated Wh is the capacity of its cells. What reaches your appliance is lower, because the inverter, the battery management system and a reserve at the bottom of the pack all take a share. The figures below were measured by named labs running each station from full to empty:

StationRatedDeliveredLoad / lab
BLUETTI AC1801,152 Wh1,030 Wh350 W, StorageReview; 1,360 Wh from the wall to refill, so 1,030 ÷ 1,360 = 76% round trip
BLUETTI AC1801,152 Wh980 Wh (950 Wh after 3 months in a garage)~380 W dehumidifier, Outdoor Life
ALLPOWERS S2000 Pro1,500 Wh (2023 unit)920 Wh350 W, StorageReview
EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus1,024 Wh910 Wh; 1,180 Wh in to rechargeStorageReview (load not stated)

EcoFlow DELTA 31,024 Wh900 Wh~380 W, Outdoor Life
Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 21,024 Wh850 Wh~250 W, Notebookcheck (EU 230 V unit)

Small loads come out worse. On a ~34 W grow light, Outdoor Life got 620 Wh from the AC180 over 15.1 h and 530 Wh from the DELTA 3 over 13.9 h, about half the rating. The inverter's own draw counts for more when the load is small.

Wiring the AC180 kit. BLUETTI rates the AC180's solar input at 500 W max, 12–60 V Voc and 10 A. Two 200 W panels in parallel run at a single panel's voltage, which is well under the 40 V needed, so the 10 A cap holds them below 400 W. Wired in series, the voltages add and the pair can deliver its full rating. Keep the series total under 60 V Voc, and use two panels of the same model. If you take the cheaper route ({buy:bluetti-ac180-200w-solar-kit}), BLUETTI's variant listing doesn't name the kit's 200 W panel, so check that it is an SP200L before adding a second one.

The Anker kit. Anker's US page lists the C1000 Gen 2 + 400 W bifacial bundle as shipping from early December, but showed no price on 2026-11-08, so it isn't in the priced table. The C1000 Gen 2 takes 14.5 A only from 29–60 V. Below 29 V it takes 8.2 A, which caps a panel at 28 V × 8.2 A = 230 W. A 400 W panel therefore has to run at 29 V or more to deliver its full output.
